Topics: ETL and Data Warehousing - OLAP Design
A. ETL Foundations
ETL vs ELT: concepts, trade-offs, use cases
Must Have: Understands the difference between ETL and ELT and when each is appropriate.
Desirable: Chooses the right pattern based on data volume, latency, and infrastructure.
Advanced/ Best: Designs hybrid ETL/ELT architectures that leverage pushdown transformations efficiently.

Topics: Batch vs streaming/incremental loads
Must Have: Knows how batch jobs differ from streaming and incremental updates.
Desirable: Implements incremental updates using timestamps or change flags.
Advanced/ Best: Designs near real-time streaming pipelines integrated with batch layers for low latency.

Topics: Data ingestion: files (CSV, JSON, Parquet), APIs, S3 buckets, databases
Must Have: Loads data from various file formats and APIs into a staging area.
Desirable: Automates ingestion pipelines from multiple heterogeneous sources.
Advanced/ Best: Builds scalable, fault-tolerant ingestion systems with parallelism and schema inference.

Topics: ETL transformations: cleansing, validation, enrichment, deduplication
Must Have: Cleans and validates data manually within ETL scripts.
Desirable: Implements reusable transformation modules for consistency and automation.
Advanced/ Best: Designs enterprise-grade transformation frameworks with metadata-driven validation.

Topics: Error handling, logging, and monitoring in pipelines
Must Have: Handles and logs basic ETL job errors.
Desirable: Adds structured logging and alerts for job failures.
Advanced/ Best: Implements centralized monitoring with observability dashboards and automated recovery.

Topics: Metadata management & data lineage tracking
Must Have: Records metadata manually or via naming conventions.
Desirable: Uses tools or frameworks to track lineage and metadata automatically.
Advanced/ Best: Integrates metadata and lineage into orchestration and governance systems for full traceability.

Topics: Scalability: processing small vs large datasets efficiently
Must Have: Runs ETL jobs for small-to-medium datasets efficiently.
Desirable: Tunes transformations and joins for performance on larger datasets.
Advanced/ Best: Designs elastic ETL pipelines optimized for distributed and cloud-scale data processing.

Topics: B. Data Modeling for Warehousing
OLTP vs OLAP: transactional vs analytical systems
Must Have: Understands differences between OLTP and OLAP workloads.
Desirable: Models data appropriately for analytical versus transactional use.
Advanced/ Best: Designs hybrid architectures integrating OLTP and OLAP with minimal latency (HTAP).

Topics: Dimensional modeling basics: Star schema
Must Have: Knows what a star schema is and when to use it.
Desirable: Designs star schemas with clear fact and dimension separation.
Advanced/ Best: Builds complex, optimized star schemas supporting high concurrency analytics.

Topics: Dimensional modeling basics: Snowflake schema
Must Have: Understands snowflake schema structure and normalization trade-offs.
Desirable: Implements snowflake schemas for reusable dimension hierarchies.
Advanced/ Best: Optimizes snowflake schemas for performance and query efficiency at scale.

Topics: Dimensional modeling basics: Fact tables & dimension tables
Must Have: Identifies and creates fact and dimension tables for analysis.
Desirable: Defines appropriate keys and relationships for joins.
Advanced/ Best: Designs multi-fact models with conformed dimensions and surrogate key strategies.

Topics: Slowly Changing Dimensions (SCD Types 1–3)
Must Have: Understands the concept of SCDs and the difference between types.
Desirable: Implements SCD Type 1 and Type 2 logic in ETL workflows.
Advanced/ Best: Automates SCD handling using framework-based or CDC-driven architectures.

Topics: Data mart vs enterprise data warehouse vs data lake vs lakehouse (Delta, Iceberg, Hudi)
Must Have: Knows the purpose of data marts, warehouses, and lakes.
Desirable: Differentiates storage and governance models across architectures.
Advanced/ Best: Designs hybrid lakehouse architectures integrating streaming and ACID capabilities.

Topics: Medallion architecture (bronze, silver, gold layers)
Must Have: Understands the purpose of layered data processing.
Desirable: Implements basic medallion layers for staging, refined, and curated data.
Advanced/ Best: Designs scalable medallion architectures with data quality checks and audit control at each layer.

Topics: C. Performance Engineering
Partitioning strategies (range, hash, composite)
Must Have: Knows what partitioning is and its purpose in performance.
Desirable: Implements range or hash partitioning for large tables.
Advanced/ Best: Designs multi-level composite partitioning strategies for massive-scale datasets.

Topics: Clustering/distribution keys & sort keys
Must Have: Understands how clustering or distribution affects performance.
Desirable: Applies sort and distribution keys to optimize queries in DWH systems.
Advanced/ Best: Tunes and rebalances distribution strategies for workload patterns dynamically.

Topics: Indexing strategies in OLAP vs OLTP systems
Must Have: Knows the difference between indexes used in OLTP and OLAP.
Desirable: Designs and maintains indexes to balance performance and cost.
Advanced/ Best: Implements adaptive indexing and columnar optimization for analytical workloads.

Topics: Aggregation & summary tables
Must Have: Builds simple aggregate tables for reporting.
Desirable: Automates summary table generation to speed up analytics.
Advanced/ Best: Designs materialized views and incremental aggregates for large-scale reporting systems.

Topics: CDC (Change Data Capture) concepts
Must Have: Understands the concept of tracking changes in data sources.
Desirable: Implements basic CDC using timestamps or log-based triggers.
Advanced/ Best: Designs full CDC pipelines using Debezium, Kafka, or database-native replication.

Topics: Optimizing query performance for large-scale analytics
Must Have: Writes efficient queries with basic indexing and partition awareness.
Desirable: Uses caching, pruning, and aggregation techniques for faster queries.
Advanced/ Best: Designs cost-based optimization strategies leveraging distributed query engines.

Topics: D. Data Warehouse Practices
Designing staging, raw, and curated layers
Must Have: Separates raw and processed data logically in ETL workflows.
Desirable: Implements layered data storage with clear quality checks.
Advanced/ Best: Designs scalable, versioned multi-layer architectures with governance and validation.

Topics: Schema evolution handling (additive vs breaking changes)
Must Have: Understands the impact of schema changes on pipelines.
Desirable: Handles additive schema changes gracefully.
Advanced/ Best: Automates schema evolution detection and reconciliation across layers.

Topics: Data lineage tracking tools (e.g., OpenLineage, built-in cloud features)
Must Have: Documents lineage manually using metadata or notes.
Desirable: Uses basic lineage tools integrated with orchestration platforms.
Advanced/ Best: Implements full lineage capture integrated with cataloging and observability systems.

Topics: Security and access controls (RBAC, row-level security, column masking)
Must Have: Applies simple role-based permissions in databases.
Desirable: Implements row- and column-level security for sensitive data.
Advanced/ Best: Designs enterprise-grade governance frameworks with dynamic masking and policy automation.

Topics: Auditing & compliance considerations (GDPR, HIPAA basics for DWH)
Must Have: Understands compliance and data privacy fundamentals.
Desirable: Applies anonymization and audit logging to meet compliance.
Advanced/ Best: Designs compliance-driven data architectures with automated policy enforcement.

Topics: Cost management in large-scale data pipelines
Must Have: Tracks compute and storage costs manually.
Desirable: Uses monitoring to optimize resource utilization.
Advanced/ Best: Designs cost-aware architectures leveraging auto-scaling and query optimization.

Topics: E. Cloud Data Warehouses
Snowflake (Virtual warehouses, scaling, separation of compute/storage, Time travel & zero-copy cloning, Query optimization and caching, Cost considerations)
Must Have: Runs basic queries and understands virtual warehouse concepts.
Desirable: Tunes performance using caching and warehouse scaling.
Advanced/ Best: Designs cost-efficient Snowflake architectures leveraging zero-copy cloning and time travel.

Topics: Amazon Redshift (Distribution keys, sort keys, Spectrum, Concurrency scaling)
Must Have: Runs basic Redshift queries and loads data into clusters.
Desirable: Uses sort/distribution keys and Spectrum for external data.
Advanced/ Best: Designs scalable Redshift workloads with concurrency scaling and WLM optimization.

Topics: Cloud-native elasticity vs static provisioning
Must Have: Understands the difference between fixed and elastic resources.
Desirable: Configures auto-scaling and on-demand compute in the cloud.
Advanced/ Best: Designs multi-cluster, auto-scaling architectures for peak workloads efficiently.

Topics: Cross-cloud data sharing & federation concepts
Must Have: Understands data sharing and cross-cloud basics.
Desirable: Implements basic data sharing between cloud platforms.
Advanced/ Best: Designs federated architectures enabling secure, cross-cloud analytics and governance.

Topics: F. Buildable Project Requirements (Capstone)
Design and implement a complete ETL → DWH pipeline
Must Have: Builds a simple ETL pipeline loading data into a warehouse.
Desirable: Automates ingestion, transformation, and schema design workflows.
Advanced/ Best: Designs enterprise-grade ETL/DWH systems with orchestration, CI/CD, and monitoring.

Topics: Ingest from multiple sources (files, APIs, database extracts)
Must Have: Extracts data manually from diverse sources.
Desirable: Builds automated ingestion pipelines from multiple origins.
Advanced/ Best: Designs scalable, fault-tolerant ingestion frameworks with incremental updates.

Topics: Load into staging layer → apply transformations → load curated data
Must Have: Implements basic staging and transformation sequence.
Desirable: Automates multi-layer ETL with logging and checkpoints.
Advanced/ Best: Designs modular, metadata-driven multi-stage pipelines with recovery logic.

Topics: Build star schema with fact & dimension tables
Must Have: Creates fact and dimension tables manually.
Desirable: Builds star schemas programmatically within pipelines.
Advanced/ Best: Designs dynamic schema generation with surrogate keys and conformed dimensions.

Topics: Implement SCD for selected dimensions
Must Have: Handles SCD Type 1 updates.
Desirable: Implements SCD Type 2 logic in transformation layers.
Advanced/ Best: Automates multi-type SCD handling using frameworks or CDC.

Topics: Add partitioning & materialized views for optimization
Must Have: Adds partitions manually for performance.
Desirable: Automates partition creation and manages refreshable materialized views.
Advanced/ Best: Designs self-tuning partition and materialized view strategies for query optimization.

Topics: Deploy pipeline with orchestration (Airflow/Prefect/dbt)
Must Have: Orchestrates ETL steps manually or with simple schedulers.
Desirable: Builds DAGs in Airflow or Prefect for dependency management.
Advanced/ Best: Designs production-grade orchestration with task retries, lineage, and dynamic DAG generation.

Topics: Demonstrate lineage tracking, logging, monitoring, and RBAC
Must Have: Logs and documents job runs manually.
Desirable: Integrates logging and RBAC into orchestration tools.
Advanced/ Best: Builds fully auditable, monitored pipelines integrated with centralized lineage tools.

Topics: Deploy on Snowflake or Redshift (simulate cost/performance trade-offs)
Must Have: Runs basic ETL and queries on cloud data warehouse.
Desirable: Compares performance and cost trade-offs between configurations.
Advanced/ Best: Designs optimized, scalable cloud DWH deployments balancing cost, concurrency, and performance.
